title: Events and Messaging Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit event ownership, delivery contracts, providers, and verification.
priorKnowledge: Read the events and messaging journey.
owner: Framework event, EMS provider, and NEMS distribution contracts
summary: Each event defines its owner, stable type/version, context, delivery model, consumer behavior, failure policy, observability, and compatibility contract.

sections.heading: Authority and event design
items: An event describes a completed or durable business fact owned by its source module; it is not an unauthenticated command or replacement for authoritative persistence.
Define stable name, version, owner, publication point, tenant context, minimal schema, classification, consumers, delivery expectation, retention, and compatibility.
Use references instead of copying large or sensitive records, and require consumers to retrieve and authorize current details through the owning service.

sections.heading: Delivery lifecycle
items: Publish only after the authoritative transition required by the contract, using outbox or equivalent coordination where loss between persistence and transport is unacceptable.
Consumers acknowledge after idempotent processing, track event identity, tolerate redelivery, and make ordering assumptions only inside a declared partition or key.
Retries use bounded backoff; exhausted messages enter an observable failed or dead state with replay and reconciliation procedures.

sections.heading: Provider and extension boundary
items: nEvent owns normalized publish, subscribe, serialization, lifecycle, and error contracts; adapters own broker connections, destinations, acknowledgements, batching, and vendor mapping.
Callers never import a broker SDK or select arbitrary destinations. Provider activation, endpoints, TLS, credentials, limits, and fallback use layered configuration and secret references.
A new adapter registers capabilities and proves compatibility without changing business event definitions or adding a second dispatcher.

sections.heading: Operations and recovery
items: Monitor publish and consume latency, backlog, redelivery, failure, dead state, connection, partition, and drain using bounded tenant-safe dimensions.
Test duplicate, reorder, consumer crash, broker outage, reconnect, poison message, schema evolution, replay, backpressure, shutdown, security, load, and upgrade.
Replay never bypasses current authorization or idempotency and records actor, selection, reason, attempt, and outcome for audit.

sections.heading: Event checklist
items: Owner, name, version, active state, source, target, tenant, trace, and schema.
Publication point and authoritative state transition.
Local, transported, persisted, replayable, or best-effort delivery.
Ordering, acknowledgement, idempotency, retry, dead/failed state, and recovery.
Payload minimization, authorization, retention, masking, and compatibility.

sections.heading: Provider checklist
items: Connection, destinations, serialization, acknowledgement, redelivery, ordering, batching, backpressure, and limits.
Readiness, reconnect, failover, diagnostics, drain, and close.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, load, failure, security, recovery, upgrade, and regression tests.
Document capacity, service objectives, alerts, replay authorization, supported versions, and incident procedure.
